title: Right-derived connecting maps agree with the derived triangle
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], let $\mathcal A$ have enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be left exact and additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For a short exact sequence $S:0\to A\to B\to C\to0$, define the connecting maps on the right derived functors $R^nv$ by a horseshoe injective resolution of $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] and the long exact cohomology sequence of the resulting short exact sequence of complexes [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. Under the canonical identifications $R^nv(X)\cong H^n(Rv(X[0]))$ [lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification], these connecting maps are the homology connecting maps [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] of the distinguished triangle [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] obtained by applying the right derived functor $Rv$ (an exact functor of triangulated categories) to the distinguished triangle $A[0]\to B[0]\to C[0]\to A[0][1]$ of $S$ [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle].

source.place: Tags 05TE and 015B: the canonical delta-functor from the derived category, compared with the injective-resolution construction

proof.text: Choose the horseshoe resolution $H=(I_A^\bullet,I_B^\bullet,I_C^\bullet,\alpha,\beta)$ of $S$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] and [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses]. Since each $I_A^n$ is injective, each degreewise short exact sequence splits; choose $\pi^n,s^n$. The degreewise-split connecting-morphism lemma gives the chain map $\delta=\pi d_{I_B}s:I_C^\bullet\to I_A^\bullet[1]$, and the complex long exact sequence gives the horseshoe maps after applying $v$.

The degreewise-split triangle node [lem-weil-pbc-degreewise-split-derived-triangle] identifies $I_A^\bullet\to I_B^\bullet\to I_C^\bullet\xrightarrow{\delta}I_A^\bullet[1]$ with the cone triangle (whose third map is $-p$) and hence fixes the sign. By the connecting-formula node [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-connecting-formula], the homology connecting map of $0\to v(I_A^\bullet)\to v(I_B^\bullet)\to v(I_C^\bullet)\to0$ is represented on a cocycle $z$ by $v(\pi^{n+1}d_{I_B} s^n z)$.

source.place: Tag 014Q; Homology Tag 011J (with Tag 0117 for the long exact sequence)

proof.text: The injective resolutions $s_A:A\to I_A^\bullet$, $s_B:B\to I_B^\bullet$, $s_C:C\to I_C^\bullet$ of the horseshoe, regarded as morphisms of complexes $A[0]\to I_A^\bullet$, $B[0]\to I_B^\bullet$, $C[0]\to I_C^\bullet$, are quasi-isomorphisms [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and satisfy $\alpha^0s_A=s_Bf$, $\beta^0s_B=s_Cg$ [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor]; so $Q(s_A),Q(s_B),Q(s_C)$ are isomorphisms of $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and with $w':=Q(s_A)[1]^{-1}\circ Q(\delta)\circ Q(s_C):C[0]\to A[0][1]$ the triple $(Q(s_A),Q(s_B),Q(s_C))$ is an isomorphism from the triangle $A[0]\xrightarrow{f}B[0]\xrightarrow{g}C[0]\xrightarrow{w'}A[0][1]$ to the distinguished triangle $I_A^\bullet\to I_B^\bullet\to I_C^\bullet\xrightarrow{\delta}I_A^\bullet[1]$ of Step 2. Hence the former triangle is distinguished (distinguished triangles are closed under isomorphism [def-weil-triangulated-category]). Moreover $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(A[0][1],C[0])=0$: as $C[0]\cong I_C^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ and $I_C^\bullet$ is K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], this group is $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(A[0][1],I_C^\bullet)$ [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], and a morphism of complexes from a complex concentrated in degree $-1$ to a complex concentrated in degrees $\ge0$ is zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-triangle-morphism-extension](3) the third morphism completing $A[0]\xrightarrow{f}B[0]\xrightarrow{g}C[0]$ to a distinguished triangle is therefore unique, so $w'$ is the morphism $w$ of the triangle of $S$ of [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle]: $w=Q(s_A)[1]^{-1}\circ Q(\delta)\circ Q(s_C)$ with $\delta=\pi d_{I_B}s$ of Step 1, with no sign.

proof.text: Compute $Rv$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] with the K-injective resolutions $A[0]\to I_A^\bullet$, $B[0]\to I_B^\bullet$, $C[0]\to I_C^\bullet$ of Step 3 (K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]) and $A[0][1]\to I_A^\bullet[1]$, so that $Rv(X[0])=v(I_X^\bullet)$ and the shift isomorphism $\sigma_{A[0]}$ is the identity of $v(I_A^\bullet)[1]=v(I_A^\bullet[1])$ (both differentials are $-v(d)$). By Step 3 the morphism of resolutions representing $w$ is $\delta$, so $Rv(w)=v(\delta)$, and $Rv$ carries the triangle of $S$ to the distinguished triangle $v(I_A^\bullet)\to v(I_B^\bullet)\to v(I_C^\bullet)\xrightarrow{v(\delta)}v(I_A^\bullet)[1]$ of $D^+(\mathcal B)$. Its homology connecting map [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] is $H^n(v(\delta))$ followed by $H^n(v(I_A^\bullet)[1])=H^{n+1}(v(I_A^\bullet))$, the identity on cocycles since $(K[1])^n=K^{n+1}$ with differential $-d$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; it sends the class of a cocycle $z$ to the class of $v(\pi^{n+1})v(d_{I_B})v(s^n)z$, which by Step 2 is the horseshoe connecting map $\partial^n_H$. Transporting by the canonical identifications $\theta_X^n$ of [lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification], induced by $Rv(X[0])\cong v(I_X^\bullet)$, gives $\delta_S^n=\theta_A^{n+1}\circ\partial_S^n\circ(\theta_C^n)^{-1}$, which is the asserted agreement.
